whatsHappening.background: Lebanon is facing a major humanitarian crisis driven by renewed large-scale fighting, layered on top of years of economic collapse, displacement, and damage from earlier conflict. Cross-border fire along the Blue Line began escalating on October 8, 2023, a ceasefire took effect on November 27, 2024, and hostilities intensified sharply again on March 2, 2026. The result has been mass displacement, civilian deaths, pressure on hospitals, damaged infrastructure, and worsening food insecurity.

timeline.description: UNIFIL reported rockets fired from southeast Lebanon toward Israeli-occupied territory, marking the start of the current cross-border escalation.
A ceasefire took effect between Israel and Lebanon under a US-brokered truce as the war caused major damage and losses in Lebanon.
OCHA, WHO, and UN updates reported renewed hostilities, mass displacement, rising casualties, and growing humanitarian need.

image.alt: Civilians looking at destroyed buildings in Lebanon

civilianImpact.experiences: People have been killed, injured, displaced, and cut off from health care, food, shelter, and basic services. Families are living in overcrowded shelters or with host communities, while women, children, older adults, and people with disabilities face especially high risks. Hospitals and primary health centers have been damaged or closed, which makes treatment harder even for people with chronic illnesses or routine medical needs. Food insecurity was already widespread, and the latest fighting is making it worse.
